title: Transient dynamics of stall and reattachment at low Reynolds number
relevance: Direct force and PIV measurements on an aerofoil and wing at chord Reynolds numbers 8×10^4–1×10^5 during pitch and Reynolds-number transients. It resolves lift delay, bubble bursting and formation, and spanwise flow development at a useful small-aircraft Reynolds range.
limitations: Idealized wind-tunnel models rather than a complete RC airplane. The numerical data are available from the corresponding author on request; the paper's supplementary movies are not raw force or PIV datasets.
access: Open-access Cambridge PDF downloaded. PDF signature, title and searchable text verified. Article states data are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request; no public numeric dataset was found.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated on the article page.
read_depth: Checked full PDF text, abstract, experimental methods, selected results, conclusion and data-availability statement. Did not digitize the plotted series.

title: Laminar separation bubble formation and bursting on a finite wing
relevance: Measures lift and PIV on a rectangular NACA 0018 wing and a two-dimensional baseline while a free-stream ramp moves the flow between reattached-bubble and stalled states. It shows the finite wing's lift changes more gradually and with less hysteresis than the two-dimensional airfoil, a useful check against treating section stall as whole-wing stall.
limitations: The transition cases are approximately Re_c 5.4×10^4–8.1×10^4 and use an idealized wind-tunnel wing. The supporting measurements are available from the authors on request, not as a public time-series archive.
access: Open-access Cambridge PDF downloaded. PDF signature, title and searchable text verified. Article states data are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated on the article page.
read_depth: Checked full PDF text, abstract, experimental methods, selected Reynolds-number cases, results, conclusion and data-availability statement. Did not digitize the plotted series.

title: All you need is time to generalise the Goman–Khrabrov dynamic stall model
relevance: A primary model study that replaces fitted Goman–Khrabrov time constants with pitch-rate and vortex-shedding time scales, then compares predictions against three experimental datasets. Its NACA 0018 case at Re_c=75,000 is the closest reported condition to typical RC-wing Reynolds numbers; the NACA 0015 and OA209 cases extend the comparison to higher Reynolds numbers.
limitations: This is model validation against previously published lift measurements, not a new experiment or a raw-data release. The Re_c=75,000 comparison uses the Le Fouest et al. 2021 ramp-up dataset already indexed in the adjacent low-Re collection; its printed dimensional setup/Re inconsistency remains unresolved, so this point should not be treated as independent physical calibration.
access: Open-access Cambridge PDF downloaded. PDF signature, title and searchable text verified. No separate public time-series dataset was found.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated in the article.
read_depth: Checked the full PDF text, model equations, the three experimental comparison cases, error metrics and conclusions. Did not re-fit the model or reconstruct the experimental histories.

title: Direct force measurements of a two-dimensional airfoil undergoing dynamic stall
relevance: The repository abstract describes sinusoidal NACA 0012 tests at Re_c=7.7×10^4, with direct lift/drag forces and water-tunnel flow visualization across pre-stall, light-stall and deep-stall cases. Four reduced frequencies from 0.005 to 0.04 make it a close Reynolds-number and transient-load comparator.
limitations: A two-dimensional section experiment, not a finite wing or complete aircraft. The measured histories are summarized in the thesis record, but no separate data archive was identified.
access: PolyU's official record exposes the thesis metadata and links to its full-text record. That linked host returned an interactive access challenge during retrieval; no file was saved and the challenge was not bypassed.
license: The PolyU repository states that items are all rights reserved unless otherwise indicated; no separate thesis license was found.
read_depth: Read the official repository abstract and case summary only. The thesis PDF was not retrieved, so its figures and detailed methods were not independently inspected.

title: Unsteady Aerodynamics of Wing-Gust Encounters
relevance: Primary water-towing-tank experiments on flat-plate wings combine force, PIV and dye visualization. The thesis covers top-hat gust ratios 0.2, 0.5 and 1.0 at Re_c=5,000–40,000 and distinguishes the measured gust-vortex force from classical added-mass terms; it provides a broad, low-Re benchmark for transient loads and gust-layer interactions.
limitations: Flat-plate models and Reynolds numbers below many conventional RC-aircraft conditions; no free-flight aircraft or open raw-log archive was found. The thesis and the 2018 conference paper below share this research programme and should not be counted as independent experimental campaigns.
access: Full Cambridge repository PDF downloaded; PDF signature and title verified. Repository metadata states all rights reserved; retained locally only.
license: All rights reserved, as stated in Cambridge repository metadata; public access does not imply redistribution permission.
read_depth: Checked the full searchable thesis, abstract, experimental summary and selected methods/results sections. Did not reprocess or digitize the time histories.

title: Response of a Flat Plate Wing to a Transverse Gust at Low Reynolds Numbers
relevance: A focused paper from the Cambridge water-tank programme above. It measures a flat-plate wing entering a top-hat gust with strength comparable to flight speed and documents the lift/drag transient, leading-edge vortex and gust-shear-layer deformation; linear gust theory fits entry better than exit.
limitations: The plate and water-tank scaling are idealized, and the paper's principal GR=1 case is an extreme gust rather than ordinary atmospheric turbulence. It overlaps the 2019 thesis and is a companion publication, not another independent dataset.
access: Public Cambridge-hosted copy downloaded. PDF signature, first-page title and authors verified; the local copy is not redistributed.
license: No reuse license was stated on the accessible university copy; public access is not taken as redistribution permission.
read_depth: Checked title page, abstract and selected experimental/results text. The broader case matrix was checked against the companion thesis; no data were digitized.

title: Physics of gust response mitigation in open-loop pitching manoeuvres
relevance: Compares three prescribed pitch manoeuvres in transverse gusts using measured force, pitching moment and PIV. It links lift mitigation to leading-edge-vortex detachment, gust exit flow and added-mass contributions, providing transient wing-response evidence for low-order model structure.
limitations: The experiment uses a flat-plate wing in a water tow tank at Re_c=10,000, far below typical fixed-wing RC conditions. It is a mechanism and model-structure comparator, not direct RC coefficient calibration; no separate raw-data archive was linked from the repository record.
access: Open-access JFM article downloaded from the University of Maryland repository. PDF signature and searchable title verified.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated in the paper.
read_depth: Read the abstract, experimental setup, force decomposition and selected results/conclusions; did not transcribe plotted histories.

title: Controlling upwards and downwards gust loads on aerofoils by pitching
relevance: Tests model-derived pitch profiles against measured force and flow in upward and downward top-hat gusts at Re_c=25,000, gust ratios 0.5 and 1.0, and initial incidences up to 45°. The paper reports strong primary-load reduction over many cases and also exposes an unmitigated secondary lift peak after gust exit.
limitations: A glass flat-plate model in water with an effective aspect-ratio arrangement, not a complete RC airplane. The primary result is a gust-control maneuver; secondary peaks and highly separated high-incidence cases are not reliably removed. No raw series were found outside the paper.
access: Open-access Springer PDF downloaded. PDF signature, title and text verified.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated in the paper.
read_depth: Checked the full searchable PDF, abstract, experimental conditions and selected mitigation/results sections. Did not digitize the plotted traces.

title: Experimental mitigation of large-amplitude transverse gusts via closed-loop pitch control
relevance: Demonstrates real-time lift feedback in a water-tank gust encounter and reports force/flow measurements for gust ratios 0.25–0.71, up/down gusts and reference incidences from 0° to 15°. It is useful for checking control-loop timing and whether pitching changes the separated-flow response, not only the attitude response.
limitations: The flat-plate wing and Re_c=10,000 experiment are much lower in Reynolds number than most RC aircraft. This overlaps the University of Maryland gust rig and model used in the 2022 paper, though the closed-loop experiment is a distinct control case. The paper provides plotted results but no separate raw-data archive.
access: Public arXiv author manuscript downloaded; PDF signature and title verified. It is the manuscript for the cited APS journal article.
license: No separate redistribution license was identified for the public arXiv copy; local retention does not imply redistribution permission.
read_depth: Checked the arXiv abstract, full-text experimental setup, gust matrix and selected closed-loop results. Did not digitize the histories.

title: Unsteady aerodynamics of a wing in a novel small-amplitude transverse gust generator
relevance: Pairs phase-locked lift measurements with PIV for a NACA 0012 rectangular wing (0.23 m chord, aspect ratio 10) exposed to periodic small-amplitude transverse gusts. It shows how separated-flow hysteresis and lift loss depend on effective incidence and reduced frequency, complementing the library's large top-hat gust encounters.
limitations: The gust generator produces a standing-wave-like disturbance rather than a gust convected over a flying aircraft. A chord-based Reynolds number was not explicit in the checked methods text, so this is a transient-response comparator rather than an exact RC-Re coefficient source. No public raw force/PIV archive was found.
access: Open-access Springer PDF downloaded. PDF signature, title and searchable text verified.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), stated in the paper.
read_depth: Checked full PDF text, abstract, model dimensions, measurement methods and selected separated-flow results; Reynolds-number value and raw-data availability were not established from the inspected text.

title: Unsteady Aerodynamics Open Data Set
relevance: An openly downloadable selected data collection from four wind-tunnel programmes: Glasgow NACA 0015/0030 dynamic stall, NREL/OSU sections, CENER NACA 64-418 pitch/flap tests and ForWind tailored inflow. It supplies time-dependent experimental data for force-response and unsteady-model comparisons; the repository also lists pressure and force NetCDF files.
limitations: This is a selected multi-facility dataset for wind-energy sections, not a single controlled RC-wing campaign or original sensor-voltage archive. Reynolds number and processing context must be matched to each contributing study. The Zenodo record did not display a reuse license.
access: Downloaded the official 3.2 MB ASCII archive from Zenodo. ZIP integrity test passed. No license was displayed on the record; the local copy is not redistributed.
license: No license stated on the Zenodo record inspected; public download is not treated as a redistribution grant.
read_depth: Read repository metadata and program descriptions; verified archive CRCs, member list and a representative CENER ASCII header/rows (Time, AoA, Flap, Cl, Cdp, Cm). Did not parse every history or execute notebooks.

title: Unsteady Aerodynamic Characteristics of a High-Performance Pitching Airfoil under Light Dynamic Stall at Low Reynolds Number
relevance: A recent direct experiment comparing an Ishii profile with NACA 0012 at Re_c=50,000, with synchronized force coefficients and PIV over reduced frequencies 0.01–0.10. This is a close low-Re section test for load hysteresis, stall recovery and pitching-moment response.
limitations: The publisher states the experimental data are available on request, not as a public dataset. It is a two-dimensional section experiment and cannot establish a complete RC wing or airplane response.
access: The publisher page marks the article open access and lists a Creative Commons license. The official PDF endpoint returned HTTP 403 during retrieval; no copy was saved and no alternate endpoint was used.
license: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0), indicated by DOI metadata; exact terms were not inspected in the blocked PDF.
